judge.voice: Okay, it was quick, about seven minutes, and the tasks were my real life: suppliers, a failed batch, the director running over. I liked that. It said B2, not C1, and I can live with that, because it showed me 'much more bigger' and 'this delay make'. Fair. But I'm not sure I trust it fully. 'He want' got a pass, and nobody said a word about 'we was discussing about' or 'he don't agree', which my director actually notices. Also 'say much bigger or more big'? That second one sounds odd to me. If I'm paying attention to the details, I'd say the level is a bit generous and the corrections are thin. Still, it's faster than a school placement test and an oral. I'd try the meeting practice next. I'd tell a colleague, but I'd warn him not to expect the full list of his mistakes.

judge.voice: The meeting was exactly my work: agenda, owners, deadlines, quality. Elena sounded like a real supplier, and I was never slowed down, which I like. The two corrections were right. "We was" I know I do, and now I see why "have been waiting" is needed. But I said "I am in this company since 2015" and "He don't" and got nothing, so I wonder what it really hears. And B2 with a quote "this delay makes"? That tells me nothing. I would want it to say what in my English put me there, because my director will notice the things it skipped. Fifteen minutes is fine for me, but I would use it again only if the level had reasons. Would I recommend it? Maybe to a colleague who is less loud than me.
